root_idea.summary: The root centers on being another's brother: sharing birth, attachment, or a defining bond, with extensions to fellowship, likeness, and connection.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from siblinghood by birth or nursing to shared tribe, religion, craft, dealings, and affection; it also develops figurative senses of likeness and attachment, including the tethering object called آخِيَّةٌ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the distinct plural citation form إِخْوَةٌ.
Displayed under the normalized singular citation form أَخٌ; the QAC group also contains the Quranic plural surface form إِخْوَانٌ.
Displayed as the distinct feminine citation form أُخْتٌ.

senses.definition: A brother: a male sibling sharing one or both parents.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic group includes the inflected forms أَخُو، أَخَا، أَخِي and the plural surface form إِخْوَانٌ when the context denotes siblinghood.

senses.definition: A brother in an extended sense: a fellow of the same tribe, religion, community, commitment, or affection; also a fellow or like of another.
senses.usage_conditions: In prophetic expressions such as “their brother,” the term marks a member of the addressed people and a brother-like relation. In إِخْوَانُ الشَّيَاطِينِ it denotes fellows or counterparts, not biological siblings.

senses.definition: Siblings, especially brothers; in a kinship context, brothers and sisters.
senses.usage_conditions: This plural can refer to a group of siblings and, as in inheritance language, can include both male and female siblings.

senses.definition: Brothers joined by a bond of faith or fellowship rather than by birth.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the plural for believers joined in solidarity and shared religious identity.
The Quranic usage denotes a sister in a family or kinship relation.

senses.definition: A female fellow, associate, or counterpart; a like or corresponding thing.
senses.usage_conditions: The term may describe a person linked by righteousness or affiliation rather than birth, or a thing comparable to another in a relevant quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a brother, friend, or companion to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; it may be used of becoming or acting as a brother to one or more persons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a tethering loop or fastening for an animal and tie the animal to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II, especially with an animal as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confer a benefit that the recipient fails to acknowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare reported figurative idiom; the source notes uncertainty in the transmitted forms of the examples.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fraternize with someone, act toward him in a brotherly manner, or unite two things as fellows or corresponding pairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III; the reciprocal or pairing sense may apply to persons or things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become brothers, friends, companions, or the like to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI reciprocal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To adopt someone as a brother or call him brother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V with a person as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, pursue, endeavor after, or strive to attain a thing or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V; the pursuit is explained by analogy with one brother seeking another. تَوَخَّى is reported as more common in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Brotherhood, fraternity, or the relation of brotherhood; by extension, a corresponding relation of sisterhood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun also used as an ordinary noun for the bond or relation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Conformity, similarity, combination, agreement, or unison in action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when the relation is not one of birth, including a relation of likeness or coordinated action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A foster-brother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical extension of the sibling term to a relation established through nursing rather than shared parentage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or group in a specified state or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiomatic construction such as أَخُو الشَّرِّ or أَخُو الخَيْرِ, whose interpretation depends on the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who cleaves or adheres to a quality or practice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In constructions such as أَخُو الصِّدْقِ, “one devoted to or keeping to truthfulness.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Worthy, fit, or suited for a thing; also possessed of a quality or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A prefixed-noun construction equivalent in some contexts to أَهْلٌ or ذُو, as in being worthy of trust or possessed of wealth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A recurring fever described as affecting the patient on alternating days or according to a recurring weekly pattern.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical medical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Brotherly, fraternal, or relating to a brother; also sisterly or relating to a sister.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival derivative, including relations of friendship or companionship where specified by context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dialectal variant of خِوَانٌ, distinct from its use as the plural of أَخٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dialectal identification is reported separately from the ordinary plural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A loop, rope, peg, or similar fastening set in or attached to the ground or a wall for tying an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers several closely related constructions, including a buried rope with an exposed loop and a peg or crosspiece used for tethering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of tent-rope or cord.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use equated with طُنُبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sacred or inviolable right, tie, claim, or bond to be respected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage for a protected relationship, entitlement, or means of connection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A support or remaining person or thing upon which one relies and to which one clings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use explained through the image of an animal secured to its tether; it may describe a valued surviving or representative member of a lineage.

cautions: إِخْوَةٌ and إِخْوَانٌ are both plurals associated with أَخٌ; the evidence reports a tendency for إِخْوَةٌ to denote siblings and إِخْوَانٌ to denote fellows, but also explicitly records Quranic exceptions and extensions.
One rare Form II idiom is retained because it is stated in the primary lexical evidence, although the source itself notes uncertainty in the transmitted orthography of its examples.
The QAC أَخٌ form group includes the Quranic surface plural إِخْوَانٌ, while إِخْوَةٌ is separately represented as its own QAC form group.
